caption: Target systems and training systems per leave-source-out fold. Training systems are all systems of the same separation mode in the other four source groups; those with at least 30 compounds (last column) were used to simulate calibrant protocols for training the difficulty model. METLIN SMRT belongs to the 'other sources' group; a random subsample of 15,000 of its retention times was added to the base-model training data in every fold.

Coverage, width and interval score of all window constructions for every calibrant number n and level α (RP target systems; per-system averages over 20 calibrant draws, then averaged over systems; 95 % bootstrap CI over systems). ∞: unbounded window (too few calibrants for the requested level; coverage is then trivially 1). The ablated variants are given in Table S17.

Mean coverage with 95 % bootstrap confidence intervals from resampling systems and from a cluster bootstrap over the five source folds, deviation from the nominal level 1 − α and share of systems whose coverage is more than 0.05 below nominal. A coverage of 1.000 with interval [1.000, 1.000] indicates unbounded windows (Table S2).

Paired comparison of per-system interval scores of the proposed windows with each comparator for every n and α (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction; negative differences favour the proposed windows). Comparators whose windows are unbounded at a given (n, α) are omitted.
Exploratory results with very small calibrant sets (n = 5 and 8; post hoc). ∞: unbounded window (n < 1/α − 1).

Fixed-tolerance windows (±0.25 to ±2 min, ±5 % and ±10 % of the predicted RT) and residual-based windows (±2·RMSE, ±3·RMSE of the calibrant residuals) evaluated on the same calibrant draws as the main study (post hoc), with the proposed windows, jackknife+ and the Gaussian window (α = 0.10) for reference. The column 'Systems > 0.05 below nominal' refers to the nominal level 0.90.
Mean coverage, mean interval score and median width per held-out source group (n = 20, α = 0.10).

Paired comparison of per-system interval scores of the proposed windows with three comparators within each held-out source group (n = 20, α = 0.10; negative differences favour the proposed windows; unadjusted two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests).

Mean coverage (per-system coverage within the stratum, averaged over systems) by stratum of test compounds (n = 20, α = 0.10, 20 draws). Seen/not seen: test compound present in/absent from the base-model training data; Tanimoto: maximum similarity to the training compounds; calibrant score range: range of the base-model scores of the calibrants; RT range thirds: thirds of each system's retention-time range (not thirds of the compounds).
Mean coverage by ClassyFire superclass (n = 20, α = 0.10).
Lowest stratum-level coverage of each method over the strata of Table S9 (n = 20, α = 0.10; nominal 0.90).

ClassyFire classes with the largest number of misses of the proposed 90 % windows (n = 20, first calibrant draw of each system); miss rate = misses divided by the number of test compounds of the class.

Candidate filtering with isomeric decoys (same molecular formula, different InChIKey connectivity block; n = 20, calibrant draws 0–4): mean retention of the correct structure, mean and median share of decoys eliminated, and mean numbers of test compounds with at least one decoy and of decoys per system and draw.

Paired comparison of per-system decoy elimination of the proposed windows with comparators at the same α (positive differences: the proposed windows eliminate more decoys; unadjusted two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests). Differences at the same nominal level partly reflect different retention of the correct structure (Table S13); see Table S15 for a comparison at matched retention.

Share of isomeric decoys eliminated at matched retention of the correct structure (85 % and 90 %), obtained by linear interpolation of each method's retention–elimination curve over α = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20; '–': retention level not reached at any tested α.
Retention of the correct structure and elimination of isomeric decoys by fixed-tolerance and residual-based windows (n = 20, calibrant draws 0–4; post hoc).

Ablation of the difficulty model and of the construction (n = 20, α = 0.10): median paired change in the per-system interval score relative to the full proposed model (positive = worse) with 95 % bootstrap CI, rank-biserial correlation, Holm-adjusted p of the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and mean coverage. Feature-group ablations retrain the difficulty model without that group.
Sensitivity to the hyper-parameters of the gradient-boosted difficulty model (default: 31 leaves, 400 trees; n = 20, α = 0.10, 10 calibrant draws per system).

Robustness to calibrant selection and calibrant errors (n = 20, α = 0.10; 10 calibrant draws per system in the perturbed scenarios). Noise: Gaussian noise with a standard deviation of 2 % of the RT span added to all calibrant RTs; outlier: one calibrant shifted by 10 % of the span.

Where coverage is lost under non-random calibrant selection and calibrant errors (n = 20, α = 0.10): share of test compounds whose base score lies outside the calibrant score range, and coverage inside and outside that range and for compounds eluting in the last third of the system's RT range.

Generalisation to a second base model (gradient-boosted regressor trained on METLIN SMRT only, applied to the RP target systems) and to HILIC systems (retention-order and difficulty models trained on HILIC systems of the other source groups); α = 0.10.

External validation on the NORMAN interlaboratory NTS data (37 chromatographic methods). Laboratory calibrant mix: all detected calibration chemicals of each method as calibrants, suspects as test compounds; random calibration chemicals: random subsets of the calibration chemicals as calibrants, suspects as test compounds; random compounds: calibrants drawn at random from all compounds. SASC rows apply the selection-aware factor estimated by replaying the calibrant-mix rule on RepoRT systems (post hoc).
Mean coverage by stratum of test compounds on the NORMAN data (α = 0.10) for each calibration scenario (laboratory calibrant mix: all detected calibration chemicals; random scenarios: n = 20).

Selection-aware system-level calibration (SASC) on the RepoRT target systems for three calibrant-selection rules (n = 20, α = 0.10; post hoc). The factor c is estimated per fold by replaying the rule on the training systems (Table S25).

SASC factors c by which the scaled scores are multiplied, estimated on the training systems of each fold for the proposed windows (c_P) and jackknife+ (c_J); c < 1 narrows and c > 1 widens the windows. Last row: factor applied to the NORMAN laboratory mixes, estimated on the RepoRT RP systems that contain at least 10 of the NORMAN calibration chemicals and at least 10 other compounds, with these chemicals as calibrants (each system scored with the models of its own leave-source-out fold).

Computation time on one CPU thread (benchmark system 0391): calibration of a new system (leave-one-out monotone maps and difficulty scales of the calibrants) and window computation per candidate structure. One-off training on public data: base model 4.0 min (82,924 retention times), difficulty model 5.3 s; peak memory 2660 MB.
